Past analyses of AAPL (most recent first):

[2026-07-22 | AAPL | Underweight | +3.8% | +6.2% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Trim AAPL by ~25% of existing exposure at market (~$325.89), with a second tranche into $329–$333.74 strength, and complete the cut toward 0.70–0.75x target weight if no bounce arrives within roughly 5–10 sessions or on a daily close below $322.88 on expanding volume. Do not add new long money here; re-adding requires either a controlled hold of the $314.86–$317.31 shelf with VWMA still rising, or a staged re-risk above $335 on ≥70M shares with the MACD histogram re-expanding above 2.5. Keep the core for the intact rising MA stack and strong franchise, size tactical trades 25–35% smaller given ATR $8.02 (2.46%), and commit nothing into the unresolved Q3 event. Horizon 1–3 months tactical; core re-scored post-Q3.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is not contested — the research plan, the trader, and all three analysts land on reduce; the debate is only about execution, which the neutral framing resolves. The evidence for trimming now is measurable and forward-looking: the MACD histogram collapsed 3.337 (07-17) → 1.599 (07-22), −52% in four sessions, with the MACD line rolling 8.927 → 8.712; AAPL printed lower highs ($334.99 on 07-17 → $329.00 on 07-22) with a −2.14% reversal on 07-20; and the support cushions are smaller than one risk unit — 10-EMA $322.88 is 0.92% away, VWMA $319.48 is 2.0% away, against an ATR of $8.02 (2.46%) — so ordinary volatility can break both without a thesis change. Layered on are the forward EPS headwinds the panel repeatedly flags: 17.5% tax rate as the new baseline (vs 15.5%), a 25.3% H1 buyback cut with net share count −0.71%, H1 OCF flattered by an $11.3B lower cash-tax payment and a $22.5B working-capital release that likely reverses, inventory +18% into Q3, and a $12.8B intangible build with no discrete acquisition line. After +20.25% YTD and +21.3% in 15 sessions, that March-quarter strength is already paid for, and no valuation multiple exists in the dataset to argue otherwise.

What keeps this Underweight rather than Sell/deeper de-risk is the neutral analyst's correct defense: the primary trend is fully stacked and rising (10-EMA $322.88 > 50-SMA $304.89 > 200-SMA $275.28), MACD is still above signal (8.712 vs 7.113), VWMA has climbed $300.72 → $319.48 in three weeks, price is only −2.35% off its record close, and the pullback is on shrinking volume (63.41M → 38.76M) — distribution of momentum, not of shares. That is why the conservative analyst's "take the whole trim immediately, depend on no bounce" and the aggressive analyst's full re-risk on a single $335 close both overreach. My own record reinforces the moderate path: the 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-01 AAPL Underweights (+8.3%, +7.4% raw) were wrong for trimming into a confirmed uptrend, so the fix is the neutral construction — trim modestly, execute roughly half at market and hold half for strength, complete the trim on a defined no-bounce window or a high-volume break of $322.88, and require confirmation (not price alone) before re-risking.

Data gaps stated plainly: no holdings or cash were provided, so sizing is a fraction of the caller's current AAPL weight, not a dollar amount; there are no AAPL filings past 2026-03-28, no news for July 15–20, and no sentiment or valuation multiple data, so this is a technical-plus-forward-fundamentals call. Upgrades: a controlled hold of $314.86–$317.31 with VWMA still rising, or a decisive close above $333.74–$335 on ≥70M shares with the histogram re-expanding above 2.5 (added in stages, preferably post-Q3). Downgrades: a close below $319.48 opens $310.06 then $304.89 (50-SMA); a decisive breakdown of $304.89 shifts to deeper Underweight/Sell.

**Price Target**: 318.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months tactical (spanning the pending Q3 print)

REFLECTION:
The 5-day +6.2% alpha (raw +3.8%) went against the Underweight call — trimming at $325.89 sold into strength — though five sessions cannot validate or refute a 1–3 month thesis spanning an unresolved Q3 print. What this window undercuts is the "distribution of momentum" read: the MACD histogram decay and lower highs did not translate into the high-volume break of $322.88 the plan required, and the stacked rising MA stack proved the better signal, repeating the 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-01 Underweight error (+8.3%, +7.4%). The lesson: in a fully stacked rising trend, treat momentum decay as a reason to shrink size, not to trim—require an actual close below the 10-EMA/VWMA on expanding volume as the trigger, and let the defined no-bounce window do the work rather than pre-empting it.

[2026-07-21 | AAPL | Underweight | +3.8% | +4.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL at ~327.74 — a partial de-risking trim, not an exit. If at or above standard allocation, reduce to roughly 60–65% of standard (sell ~35–40%) into the 327–334 zone ahead of the imminent Q3 FY2026 print; do not add at the Tier-1 322.22–324 zone, which the panel's own arithmetic shows is only ~1.1:1. If trimming is infeasible (tax/liquidity), the alternative is a collar — buy ~1-month 308–310 puts against calls near 340–344. For the retained core, honor downside triggers on a CLOSING basis only: 322.21 voids the short-term trend, 308.48/304.24 confirms the July breakout failed and argues for a minimal core. If flat or below standard weight, do not initiate now; wait for the print or a sub-305 test that holds with a higher low and improving volume, then start at 50–60% of standard. Horizon: 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the print.

**Investment Thesis**: The debate resolved into a trim, and the only live question was whether it should be modest (trader/neutral, ~35–40%), deeper (conservative, 45–50%), or a full Sell. The evidence supports the moderate Underweight and decisively rejects both a Hold and a Sell.

Why a trim (the deciding evidence): the reward-to-risk at 327.74 is poor by the report's own numbers — ~+5.0% to the 344.09 upper band against ~−7.2% to the 304.24 invalidation, roughly 0.7:1, and the bull's own Tier-1 322.22–324 only reaches ~1.1:1 (a coin flip). Critically, this time the bear has an actual REJECTION signal, not mere proximity to resistance: three consecutive lower highs (334.99→333.71→329.60) with two lower lows, the 10-EMA slope collapsing from +3.70 to +1.23/day, RSI diverging 79.79 (a 312.51 close) → 71.65 (a higher 333.74 close) → 64.54, the MACD histogram rolling 3.337→2.214, and the 07-21 bounce on 41.3M shares versus 61–63M on the breakout. That distinction matters because my prior AAPL lessons (2026-07-13 Underweight +3.9% alpha against; 2026-06-30/07-01 Underweights wrong by 7–8%) all lost for one reason — trimming into a confirmed uptrend on the basis of a nearby level rather than an actual failed push. That error is not being repeated here; the failed push has printed. Add the stale fundamentals (the latest hard filing is a 10-Q for the period ended 2026-03-28, accepted 2026-05-01 — four months old, predating the margin-anxiety cluster, the OpenAI suit and the fade), the cash-flow-quality flags the conservative correctly raised (roughly $30–35B of the first-half CFO beat looks like tax timing and non-trade receivable collection, AP −$12.5B, a working-capital flip, intangibles +94%, an unexplained +$14B other-liabilities jump, effective tax rate ~17.5%), and a 5:1 negative news/macro day with a GOOGL print as direct read-across and Mag-7 rotation as the exact multiple-compression mechanism for a ~33× name — and the case to reduce into the event is solid.

Why Underweight and not Sell: the business is not broken and no one in the debate successfully argued it is. Revenue +16.1%, gross margin 48.64% (+168bp), operating margin 34.02%, EPS +19.8%, ~$62B net cash, ~$129B TTM FCF, and the fully stacked, rising structure (price > 10-EMA > 50-SMA > 200-SMA, VWMA 317.27) are intact. The aggressive analyst's "heads you win, tails you win better" is overstated, as the neutral correctly noted — the 60–65% core still absorbs most of any gap and the reserve has real opportunity cost — and his rebuild-at-334.99 idea is churn (a ~2.2% round trip in a name where one ATR is 2.5%), which the trader's own plan already labels a scale-out, not an add.

Why not the conservative's 45–50%: halving the book on ambiguous data creates its own tracking-error risk, and the half-year aggregates — the reliable unit per the report — remain strong. The OpenAI suit and the "rare technical signal" are headlines with no disclosed damages, timeline or indicator, not thesis-breakers. The neutral's synthesis is the strongest read on the merits: 35–40% trim, lean to 35% if only modestly above standard or normal risk tolerance, 40% if materially above standard or a 5–6% gap cannot be tolerated.

What would change the call: a daily close above 334.99 on ≥60M shares stops the trim stance and prompts reassessment — but I explicitly reject the aggressive's automatic buy-back at 335; any rebuild must come post-print, on verified gross margin near 48%, a tax rate near 17.5% or better, normalized-but-healthy 2H cash flow and stable guidance, or on a 304–313 retest that actually holds with a higher low and improving volume — otherwise the reserve stays in cash, which is a position, not a failure. A confirmed close below 304.24 with expanding volume escalates toward a minimal core; I will not size the exit off closing-level stops alone given 2.5% daily ATR and a history of five three times in seven months — hence the optional put collar as the real gap-risk control. Explicitly missing: confirmed print date beyond "imminent," any quantified guidance, valuation multiples, options/IV pricing, insider data, and the caller's actual weight and cost basis.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months (through the Q3 FY2026 print), re-underwritten post-print

REFLECTION:
Five days delivered +4.8% alpha against the Underweight, so the directional call was wrong so far, though the one-to-three-month window into the print is far too short to judge the thesis. The window undercuts the specific claim that mattered most: the three lower highs, collapsing 10-EMA slope and MACD roll were treated as a printed failed push, yet price did not follow through lower, which is the same failure mode flagged in the 2026-07-13, 06-30 and 07-01 Underweights. The lesson is to require an actual trigger — a close below 322.21 with a lower low on expanding volume — before cutting a position inside a fully stacked rising structure, and to express the bearish view through the collar rather than selling stock when only the momentum divergence supports the trim.

[2026-07-20 | AAPL | Underweight | +3.2% | +3.6% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AAPL — this is a MODEST, position-dependent trim of existing exposure, not a short and not a full exit. Reduce by roughly one-third toward ~0.65–0.70x standard allocation at 326.59 (lean lighter, ~0.70x, if the position is right-sized and the caller can tolerate an event gap; lean toward ~0.60x only if oversized/concentrated). Put NO new capital to work at 326.59; if flat, stay flat rather than initiate a long into a binary FQ3 print. Hold the residual long with a close-based review at 311.91 (July 14 low) and cut further on a decisive close below it rather than averaging down. Rebuild in tranches only on a stabilized pullback into the 314–321 VWMA/10-EMA cluster or after the earnings event clears; add back toward full only on a confirmed close above 334.99 with the MACD histogram re-expanding. Horizon 1–3 months tactical, core re-scored at the late-July FQ3 report.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is not genuinely contested: all three risk seats converge on reducing AAPL exposure into strength at 326.59, and they differ only on magnitude (aggressive ~0.65x, neutral 0.55–0.60x, conservative 0.5x). The consensus is "reduce exposure, take partial profits," which is precisely the definition of Underweight. A Sell (full exit) is not supported because the business and trend remain structurally strong — price is still above the 10-EMA 320.98 > VWMA 314.02 > 50-SMA 303.43 > 200-SMA 274.58, the 50/200-SMAs are rising, H1 revenue grew ~16.1%, FQ2 gross margin hit 49.3%, EPS +~20%, and net cash is ~$62B. No seat produced evidence of franchise deterioration, and a fresh short is a low-reward fade of a stacked uptrend (invalidation 334.99), which even the aggressive seat rejects.

What tips the actionable call to trim NOW — and separates this from my prior AAPL Underweights that were wrong within five days — is that this is the first setup that actually prints the rejection signal those lessons told me to wait for. 2026-07-20 was a bearish reversal day at a record high: opened 333.51, failed 333.71, closed 326.59 below the prior session's 329.00 low. The MACD histogram has its first decline since the 2026-07-02 crossover (3.34 → 2.72), and RSI fell −7.8 points in a single session (71.65 → 63.87) with price +7.6% above the 50-SMA and ~19% above the 200-SMA. That is a confirmed deceleration, not mere proximity to resistance. On top of it, the star catalyst (China Apple Intelligence via Alibaba) is unquantified — no launch date, attach rate, or revenue framing from 20 of 196 records — and arrived AFTER a +21.3% run from 281.74 to 333.74, so crediting the run to the catalyst inverts causation and leaves sell-the-news risk. The reward/risk into the print is roughly 1:1: ~15.1 points upside to the Bollinger upper (341.70) versus ~14.7 points to the 311.91 stop, and the conservative seat is right that a gap can jump straight through 311.91 toward the 314.02/306.95/303.43 magnets — so the true event downside is wider than the stop implies, which is why position size, not the stop line, is the primary control.

I adopt the neutral analyst's sizing discipline and the prior-lesson guidance together: trim toward the LIGHT end (~one-third to ~0.65–0.70x) rather than the conservative 0.5x, because (a) the franchise and stacked trend are intact, (b) my own record shows repeated over-trimming into intact uptrends cost alpha (2026-06-30, 07-01, 07-13 Underweights all underperformed by 3–8% in five days), and (c) the aggressive seat's 53.5M-share down day is only ~52.6M ex-spike average, i.e., neutral evidence — not confirmed distribution. But I do not hold full size: carrying 1.0x into a binary print after a 21.3% run is an active bet on good news, and the conservative and neutral seats are correct that the buyback cut (−25.3%), the tax-rate reset to ~17.5%, R&D +32.6% against ~16% revenue, an unmodeled $12.8B intangible build, and working-capital/tax-timing flattered FCF raise the bar the FQ3 guide must clear.

Known data gaps, stated plainly rather than papered over: no valuation multiple (P/E, EV/FCF, forward estimates) is computable from the packet, so no price target is offered as thesis; no sentiment/insider data; no confirmed FQ3 gross-margin guide; no options/IV pricing to size a hedge; and no China AI attach-rate or launch-date quantification. What would change the call: a decisive close above 334.99 with the MACD histogram re-expanding upgrades toward Hold/Overweight and triggers staged adds; a close below 311.91 prompts further reduction rather than averaging down; a break of the 314.02 VWMA on expanding volume is trend damage; and FQ3 gross-margin guidance below 48% (or confirmation that the working-capital/tax tailwind reverses into OCF, or adverse channel/receivables commentary) ratifies the bear case and argues for staying light. Conversely, guide ≥48% with the operating-leverage case intact and a China AI datapoint would justify rebuilding toward full/Overweight.

**Price Target**: not provided

**Time Horizon**: 1–3 months tactical (trim); core re-scored at the late-July FQ3 print

The 5-day +3.6% alpha versus SPY went against the Underweight trim—AAPL rose 3.2%—so the directional call was wrong over this window, though five days is too short to judge a 1–3 month thesis built around the FQ3 print. It undercuts the rejection/deceleration leg, since the 2026-07-20 bearish reversal and MACD/RSI rollover did not follow through, while supporting the stacked-uptrend caution against shorting or fully exiting. Next time, in an intact stacked uptrend with my record of over-trimming, require follow-through below 311.91 before trimming and keep any pre-print trim at the light end rather than treating one reversal day as confirmation.
